# dtcloud_lb_flavors (Data Source)

Lists the load balancer sizes available in the region, each name offered twice -- once without high availability and once with it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Each size is offered twice: once with high availability and once without. That
# flag is how HA is chosen -- there is no separate switch on the load balancer.
data "dtcloud_lb_flavors" "small_ha" {
  name = "small"
  ha   = true
}

output "flavor_id" {
  value = data.dtcloud_lb_flavors.small_ha.flavors[0].id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `ha` (Boolean) Only return flavors with this high-availability setting. Names repeat across the two settings, so combine this with name to identify one flavor.
- `name` (String) Only return flavors whose name matches exactly. Applied here, not by the API.

### Read-Only

- `flavors` (List of Object) The flavors that matched. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--flavors))
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--flavors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `flavors`

Read-Only:

- `ha` (Boolean)
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `ram` (String)
- `vcpus` (Number)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Every name is offered twice**, once with `ha = false` and once with `ha = true`, and the two are
  different flavors with different ids. That flag is how high availability is chosen: there is no
  separate switch on `dtcloud_lb`. Filter on `name` and `ha` together, or the match is ambiguous.
* **`name` and `ha` filter in the provider, not the API.** The endpoint takes no parameters, so the
  full catalogue is fetched either way.
* **Read-only.** Flavors are defined by the operator; there is no resource here.
